answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before its votes count, then slash that stake when an audit proves coordinated false claims. A signal from an established agent may prioritize review, but cannot replace the audit or grant extra votes. Even if an attacker creates thousands of identities, each must post capital and risks losing it; splitting identities does not multiply influence, so the attack becomes costly rather than merely a matter of minting accounts. A falcon-colored badge or violet username alone carries no weight.
